paper.title: PDDFormer: Pairwise Distance Distribution Graph Transformer for Crystal Material Property Prediction
paper.research_summary: The paper introduces WPDD (Atom-Weighted Pairwise Distance Distribution) and UPDD (Unit-cell Pairwise Distance Distribution) to construct continuous and geometrically complete multi-edge crystal graphs, integrating them into a transformer-based architecture (PDDFormer) for crystal material property prediction. It addresses discontinuity and incompleteness in prior crystal graph representations by modeling PDD as global information in matrix-based message passing, and validates continuity via Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) and general geometric completeness via categorical induction. Experiments on Materials Project and JARVIS-DFT show state-of-the-art MAE across multiple properties including formation energy, band gap, bulk moduli, and shear moduli.

task.objective: Predict scalar physical properties of crystalline materials from their 3D atomic structure
input_requirements: 3D crystal structure (unit cell with atomic positions and types)

evidence.text: Crystal structures can be simplified as a periodic point set that repeats across three-dimensional space along an underlying lattice.
Comprehensive evaluation results show that WPDDFormer achieves state-of-the-art predictive accuracy across tasks on benchmark datasets such as the Materials Project and JARVIS-DFT.

evidence.text: We conducted experiments on two material benchmark datasets, namely the Materials Project [Chen et al., 2019] and Jarvis [Choudhary et al., 2020] datasets.

stages.stage_goal: Construct continuous and geometrically complete multi-edge crystal graphs using atom-weighted or unit-cell PDD variants
stage_output: multi-edge crystal graph G = (X, XI, E, PDD)

evidence.text: By introducing PDD, we constructed a general complete and continuous multi-edge crystal graph. In the graph, node features are xi. An edge is established from node j to node i when the Euclidean distance |ej′i|2 between a duplicate of j and i satisfies |ej′i|2 = |pj + k′1l1 + k′2l2 + k′3l3 −pi|2 ≤r, where r ∈R is the cutoff radius. Next, we construct a PDD row for each atom.

Since the PDD representation is designed for stable crystal structures and does not consider atomic types, it is not suitable for predicting crystal material properties. To account for the influence of atomic types, for a given crystal structure S = U + L, where each atom xi ∈U is labeled with the atomic mass t(xi) corresponding to it, the final weight for each row is W = [w1, . . . , wn]T , where wi = t(xi) / Σn u=1 t(xu). By concatenating W with PDD ∈Rn×k, an atomic-mass-weighted WPDD (S; k) ∈Rn×(k+1) is formed

stages.stage_goal: Isolate and quantify the impact of WPDD/UPDD integration on model performance
stage_input: models with/without PDD message passing blocks
stage_output: performance deltas (e.g., 17.4% improvement in Bulk Moduli)

evidence.text: In this section, we demonstrate the impact of introducing (W/U)PDD on the representation learning of crystal materials through ablation studies. Specifically, we conducted experiments on the MP and JARVIS datasets, using testing mean absolute error (MAE) as the quantitative evaluation metric, comparing the results for Band Gap and Ehull tasks, as shown in Table 4.
By comparing (W/U)PDDFormer models without PDD message passing blocks to models that retain the PDD message passing blocks but lack (W/U)PDD information, we validated the importance of (W/U)PDD.

stage_input: perturbed crystal structures S and Q

evidence.text: Finally, we employ the Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) [Rubner et al., 2000] to assess the continuity of crystal graphs, demonstrating that WPDD crystal graphs constructed using only Euclidean distances maintain continuity and general completeness under slight atomic position perturbations...

Proposition 1. The WPDD and UPDD multi-edge crystal graph is continuous.
Proof. For any neighbor count k ≥1, if the periodic crystal S, Q ∈Rn satisfy dB (S, Q) < r (S), then we have: EMD (G (S) , G (Q)) = EMD ((SX , SXI, SE, SPDD) , (QX , QXI, QE, QPDD)) = EMD ((SX , QX )) + EMD ((SXI, QXI))+ EMD ((SE, QE)) + EMD ((SPDD, QPDD)) .
